question: Does writing the MotionCorrection result back into ARDY's history lower or raise the cost the viewer sees, and does a longer history change that
cluster_unit: task (G = 24); seeds and offsets are paired repetitions within a task
tasks: task_geometry.ardy_offset_tasks(), relative_offset targets as M0c / M1

W1.role: native: corrected window written to history (M1 C1)

W0.role: corrected window is the output; the next window is conditioned on the uncorrected generation

grid: C0, W1, W0 x history {32, 160} x 3 offsets x 24 tasks x 3 seeds = 1296 runs; C0 and W1 at history 32 are the M1 C0 / C1 runs (432 reused, bit-identity checked in the pilot), 864 new runs

primary.endpoint: Output boundary jerk at the 0.1 s step, W0 - W1, history 32, pooled over offsets {0.1, 0.5}; cluster t interval and exact sign-flip p
primary.decision_for_M2: W0 - W1 > 0 with the interval excluding 0: writeback lowers the visible cost and M2 starts from writeback; < 0 excluding 0: M2 starts from output-only correction; otherwise both policies stay M2 arms

secondary: history interaction: (W0 - W1 at history 160) - (W0 - W1 at history 32) on boundary jerk and history consistency
end waypoint error (both corrected arms are expected at the margin)
foot sliding, common-step jerk, trunk inclination, history consistency over the last 32 history frames
wall time per arm and history length

pilot.jobs: Offset task 10, seed 20, every arm, history length and offset (18 jobs)
pilot.admission: Finite complete outputs; time within 3x estimate; frame-0 heading within 20 degrees of body forward; C0 and W1 at history 32 bit-identical to the M1 runs of the same task, seed and offset; W1 and W0 end waypoint error <= 0.055 m; W0 history differs from W1 history after the first window (history consistency differs)

conventions_not_derived.history_frames: 32 and 160, the two archived 20261024 history lengths
